newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales drop 1 pct in Aug. - realtors.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales drop 1 pct in Aug. - realtors.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes dipped by one percent in August, compared with August of 1995, the Florida Association of Realtors said Wednesday.
Year-to-date resales climbed to 87,639, an increase of 9 percent over the first eight months of last year. The median sale price rose by 5 percent over year-ago levels, to $94,800, the Realtors said.

The association said the August totals were down because many prospective buyers rushed to close earlier in the summer, in the mistaken assumption that interest rates would soon rise. Early summer resales were exceptionally strong.
The average rate of a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 8 percent, compared to 8.25 percent in July and 7.89 percent a year ago.
Among large urban areas, Jacksonville had the largest percentage increase in August, 9 percent, with 923 homes sold during the month.

Dee Bumbarger, Realtor with Buck & Buck Inc. in Jacksonville, attributed the gain to urban growth fueld by new industry and business expansion, an a growing influx of retirees. Jacksonville's year-to-date resales were up 10 percent over last year.
Among smaller markets, the Naples area saw the biggest monthly gain, 17 percent, with 160 homes sold.

Existing home resales rose by 14 percent in Panama City, 8 percent Fort Myers-Cape Coral, 7 percent in Tallahassee, 5 percent in Fort Pierce-Port St. Lucie, 3 percent in West Palm Beach-Boca Raton, 2 percent in Tampa-St. Petersburg, and one percent in Orlando.

Sales dropped by 13 percent in the Ocala and Punta Gorda area, 12 percent in Miami, 11 percent in the Fort Lauderdale area, 10 percent int he Gainesville area, 4 percent in Lakeland-Winter Haven, 3 percent in Melbourne-Titusville, and 2 percent in Pensacola, Daytona Beach and Sarasota-Bradenton.
